metadata.title: ORTHOPEDICS OSCE
metadata.subtitle: 15 Structured Stations
metadata.audienceAndScoring: Final-Year MBBS • 8 minutes per station • 20-point analytic checklist
metadata.includedMaterials: Candidate materials • Standardised scripts • Examiner guides • Learning notes
facultyNote: This manual contains exactly 15 standalone orthopedics/musculoskeletal OSCE stations developed from the teaching material supplied by the user. All patient names in the original scenarios have been changed. The source material includes non-specific neck pain, low back pain and nerve-root pain, rickets/osteomalacia, frozen shoulder, carpal tunnel syndrome, gout, knee osteoarthritis and osteoporosis. The source contains some older or locally specific prescribing statements. This manual preserves the source topics, examination structure and teaching emphasis, while medication selection, exact dose, contraindications, referral pathways and emergency management should be checked against the current approved institutional/provincial/national protocol before summative use.
assessmentDesign: Each station is designed for 8 minutes and uses a 20-point analytic checklist (10 observable items scored 0, 1 or 2).
Score 2 = clearly and independently achieved; 1 = partially achieved or achieved after a standard prompt; 0 = omitted, incorrect or unsafe.
The analytic score and global rating should be recorded independently. Use an approved standard-setting process.
Prompted items score at most 1/2. Critical safety errors require examiner review.
contents: 1. Non-Specific Neck Pain - Focused history, red-flag screening and management
2. Acute Mechanical Low Back Pain - Focused back-pain history, red flags and early management
3. Lumbar Nerve Root Pain / Sciatica - Recognition of radicular pain and neurological assessment
4. Low Back Examination - Systematic lumbar spine and lower-limb neurological examination
5. Rickets in a Child - Recognition of skeletal manifestations and investigation planning
6. Osteomalacia in an Adult - Bone pain, muscle weakness and metabolic bone assessment
7. Frozen Shoulder / Adhesive Capsulitis - Shoulder history, differential diagnosis and management
8. Shoulder Examination - Systematic shoulder examination including impingement assessment
9. Carpal Tunnel Syndrome in Pregnancy - Median nerve compression history, examination and management
10. Carpal Tunnel Hand & Wrist Examination - Focused median nerve examination and provocative testing
11. Acute Gout of the First MTP Joint - Acute monoarthritis history and management
12. Knee Osteoarthritis - Mechanical knee-pain history, examination and management
13. Knee Examination - Systematic knee Look-Feel-Move and special tests
14. Osteoporosis - DEXA Interpretation - Fragility-fracture history, DEXA interpretation and risk assessment
15. Osteoporosis Prevention & Medication Counselling - Risk reduction and safe long-term treatment counselling

stations.title: Non-Specific Neck Pain
stations.primaryCompetency: Focused history, red-flag screening and management
candidateInstructions: Mr Hamza Farooq, aged 29 years, works as a factory supervisor and reports dull left-sided neck pain extending toward the left shoulder/arm, worse when bending to inspect machinery.
Take a relevant history, address his worry about heart disease, describe a focused examination and share a management plan.
candidateHandout: The source scenario links symptoms to prolonged awkward neck posture and emphasizes neurological screening, examination of neck movement and reassurance/ergonomic advice.
The patient is particularly worried because a close relative recently died from a heart attack.
simulationScript: Opening: “Doctor, I have pain on the left side of my neck and chest area and it seems to go toward my left arm.”
Pain is dull, about 5/10, worse with bending at work and relieved by rest; no trauma, rash, pins and needles or weakness.
No exertional pain, breathlessness or other volunteered cardiac symptoms. Concern: “I am frightened this could be my heart.”
examinerInstructions: Give the candidate the station instructions at the start and assess observable performance, clinical reasoning, examination technique and safety.
Use the standard prompts only if progress stops. Prompted items score at most 1/2.
The station is grounded in the supplied teaching material. Accept clinically appropriate local equivalents and verify medication/protocol details before summative use.
keyAnswerGuide: Explore site, onset, character, radiation, severity, aggravating/relieving factors and occupational posture.
Screen neurological symptoms and relevant serious causes; clarify chest-pain features because this is the patient's main concern.
Describe inspection, palpation, cervical range of movement and upper-limb motor/neurological assessment.

Explain a likely mechanical/non-specific pattern if assessment is reassuring; discuss posture/ergonomics, activity, simple analgesia as locally appropriate, physiotherapy/occupational advice, follow-up and safety-netting.

checklist.criterion: Introduces self, confirms identity and obtains consent.
Characterises the neck/chest/arm pain systematically.
Links symptoms to posture and occupational activity without premature closure.
Screens weakness, numbness/pins and needles and other neurological symptoms.
Clarifies exertional chest pain, breathlessness and other concerning chest symptoms.
Reviews trauma, rash and relevant medical/drug history.
Describes inspection, palpation and cervical range-of-motion examination.
Assesses upper-limb power/neurological status.
Addresses the patient's cardiac worry and explains the working diagnosis clearly.
Provides ergonomic/physiotherapy/analgesia advice, follow-up and safety-netting.

candidateInstructions: Ms Sana Qureshi, aged 46 years, is a computer operator who developed severe low-back pain after lifting a heavy box in an awkward twisted position.
Take a focused history, screen for red flags and explain the initial management plan.
candidateHandout: The source scenario describes acute mechanical backache after lifting, worsened by movement and relieved by rest, with no leg radiation.
It emphasizes avoiding prolonged bed rest, maintaining activity, lifting technique, workplace ergonomics and follow-up.
simulationScript: Opening: “I hurt my back lifting a heavy box and the pain has been terrible.”
Pain is lumbar, constant, about 6/10, worse with movement, no leg radiation, weakness or sensory loss.

stations.title: Lumbar Nerve Root Pain / Sciatica
stations.primaryCompetency: Recognition of radicular pain and neurological assessment
candidateInstructions: Mr Bilal Ahmed, aged 39 years, has low-back pain radiating down one leg with intermittent numbness.
Take a focused history, describe the relevant neurological examination and outline management.
candidateHandout: The source material distinguishes nerve-root pain from uncomplicated mechanical back pain by leg radiation, numbness, reduced straight-leg raise and reflex changes.
It includes lower-limb power, reflex and sensory testing by lumbar/sacral distribution.
simulationScript: Opening: “The back pain now shoots down my right leg and sometimes my foot feels numb.”
No bladder/bowel disturbance or saddle anaesthesia; no fever or weight loss.
Pain worsens with coughing; he is worried he has a slipped disc and will need surgery.
examinerInstructions: Give the candidate the station instructions at the start and assess observable performance, clinical reasoning, examination technique and safety.

keyAnswerGuide: Clarify radicular distribution and neurological symptoms while screening cauda equina and systemic red flags.
Examine gait, lower-limb power, reflexes, dermatomal sensation and straight-leg raise as described in the source.
Explain that nerve-root pain can often improve with conservative management when no emergency features are present.
Discuss activity, analgesia, review and escalation/imaging/referral if severe, progressive, persistent or red flags develop.

stations.title: Low Back Examination
stations.primaryCompetency: Systematic lumbar spine and lower-limb neurological examination

Explain your findings and what further examination you would perform.
candidateHandout: The source uses a Look-Feel-Move sequence, spinal palpation, flexion/extension/lateral flexion/rotation, lower-limb power, straight-leg raise, knee/ankle reflexes and sensory testing.
simulationScript: Simulated patient is able to stand and walk. Mild paraspinal tenderness may be reported if asked.
No objective weakness is provided unless the examiner supplies it.

Assess lumbar movement gently and safely.
Assess lower-limb power, reflexes and sensation; perform straight-leg raise when appropriate.
Conclude with relevant additional examination and red-flag assessment.

stations.title: Rickets in a Child
stations.primaryCompetency: Recognition of skeletal manifestations and investigation planning
candidateInstructions: A 4-year-old child, Ayaan Khan, is brought by his mother because of bowed legs, delayed growth and intermittent bone discomfort.
Take a focused history, describe examination findings you would seek and outline investigations and management principles.
candidateHandout: The source lists bone pain/tenderness, bow legs, pigeon chest, rachitic rosary, spinal deformity, delayed dentition, muscle weakness and impaired growth.
It suggests assessment of calcium, phosphate, vitamin D, parathyroid hormone, liver and renal function, and attention to dietary deficiency or secondary causes.
simulationScript: Mother says: “His legs look bowed and he seems shorter than other children his age.”
If asked: limited vitamin-D/calcium-rich diet; no known chronic kidney/liver disease.
Concern: whether the deformity will be permanent.

Examine growth parameters and skeletal features described in the source.

Explain nutritional correction/supplementation and treatment of an underlying cause according to paediatric/local protocols, with follow-up.

stations.title: Carpal Tunnel Syndrome in Pregnancy
stations.primaryCompetency: Median nerve compression history, examination and management
candidateInstructions: Ms Areeba Malik, aged 30 years and pregnant, reports intermittent nocturnal pain, tingling and numbness in the hand for 4 months.
Take a focused history, examine the hand/wrist and outline management.
candidateHandout: The source describes nocturnal symptoms in the median-nerve distribution, improvement by shaking the wrist, pregnancy/obesity/hypothyroidism/wrist trauma associations and thenar wasting as an important severity feature.
It includes Phalen and Tinel tests and nerve-conduction studies when diagnosis is uncertain or severity assessment is needed.
simulationScript: Opening: “My hand keeps going numb at night and I wake up shaking it.”
Tingling affects thumb, index and middle fingers and may ache into the forearm; worse at night and in certain wrist positions.
She is pregnant. Concern: symptoms are interfering with sleep and she is dropping objects.
examinerInstructions: Give the candidate the station instructions at the start and assess observable performance, clinical reasoning, examination technique and safety.
Use the standard prompts only if progress stops. Prompted items score at most 1/2.
The station is grounded in the supplied teaching material. Accept clinically appropriate local equivalents and verify medication/protocol details before summative use.
keyAnswerGuide: Define median-distribution sensory symptoms, nocturnal pattern and functional weakness.
Review pregnancy and other associated factors in the source; ask about previous wrist injury and thyroid symptoms.
Examine thenar bulk, thumb abduction, grip and median/ulnar sensation; perform provocative tests appropriately.
Discuss night splinting and pregnancy-appropriate symptom control, with specialist assessment for weakness/thenar wasting or persistent severe disease.
